problem.statement: In Prism-based WPF apps, a view's DataContext is already null by the time it is removed from a region, so the view model reference is lost and cannot be identified or disposed, causing a memory leak.

persona.primary: WPF developer maintaining a legacy Prism-based line-of-business application

context.situation: A developer maintaining a Prism-based WPF application with tabbed/region navigation needs to dispose view models when views are removed from a region, but the framework does not preserve the VM reference at removal time.

possible_wedges.offer: A drop-in Prism RegionBehavior/NuGet package that captures the view model reference at region-add time (e.g. via attached property or WeakReference) so it can be reliably disposed on region removal, preventing the leak.
A WPF memory/leak audit tool that scans a running or built Prism application for views/VMs whose DataContext is null at removal or that never get disposed, flagging leak-prone regions.
A static analysis CLI for legacy .NET/WPF/Prism codebases that flags IDisposable view models wired via ViewModelLocator.AutoWireViewModel that have no verified disposal path on region removal.

risks: Single evidence item (n=1) from one Stack Overflow-style question; no corroborating reports yet.
No commercial intent or willingness-to-pay signal in the evidence (commercial_intent score 0.05); this reads as a free community question, not a paid-tool inquiry.
No workarounds or substitute tools mentioned, so it's unclear whether existing free community answers already resolve this well enough to kill demand for a product.
Problem is narrow and technical (a specific Prism region-behavior gap), which may only affect a subset of legacy WPF/Prism shops rather than the broader OwnAudit audience.
Unclear whether this maps well to OwnAudit's audit-tooling positioning versus being a pure dev-library fix.

cheapest_experiment.hypothesis: WPF/Prism developers hitting this null-DataContext-on-removal leak would adopt a small free drop-in fix (region behavior snippet/package) that captures the VM reference before removal so it can be disposed.
cheapest_experiment.input: Publish a free gist/NuGet micro-package implementing a RegionBehavior that snapshots the VM at add-time (via a WeakReference or attached property) and reply to the original SO thread and 1-2 similar Prism WPF leak threads with a link.
cheapest_experiment.output: Downloads/stars on the package/gist and reply engagement (comments, upvotes, follow-up questions) on the linked threads.
cheapest_experiment.commitment_event: A developer installs the package, forks/stars the gist, or explicitly asks for a paid/supported version or audit of their app for similar leaks.
cheapest_experiment.success_threshold: 20+ downloads or stars, or 3+ people asking for deeper help/paid support within 2 weeks of posting.
cheapest_experiment.failure_threshold: Fewer than 5 downloads/stars and no requests for further help after 2 weeks.
